cases.question: What hashing algorithm does Retriva use for passwords?
expected_facts: Passwords are hashed with Argon2id

cases.question: How long is a Retriva access token valid for before it expires?
expected_facts: The access token (JWT) is valid for 15 minutes

cases.question: What is the default value of the RRF_K damping constant used in Retriva's score fusion?
expected_facts: RRF_K defaults to 60

cases.question: Which embedding model does Retriva's default local setup use?
expected_facts: nomic-embed-text is the default embedding model

cases.question: How does Retriva stop one company's data from being visible to a different company's users?
expected_facts: Every domain table carries organization_id and every query filters on it

cases.question: If someone tries to guess the ID of a workspace that isn't theirs, what does the system show them?
expected_facts: A resource belonging to another org returns 404, the same as it not existing

cases.question: Why did the team pick a rank-based way of combining two search results instead of just averaging their scores?
expected_facts: Vector similarity and keyword ts_rank are on incompatible scales, so ranks are fused instead of raw scores

cases.question: What does Retriva do if the AI model that generates answers can't be reached at all?
expected_facts: Misconfiguration or an unreachable LLM fails loudly rather than silently falling back

cases.question: What does the WORKER_METRICS_PORT setting control?
expected_facts: WORKER_METRICS_PORT is the port the Celery worker's own Prometheus metrics server listens on

cases.question: What is websearch_to_tsquery used for in Retriva?
expected_facts: websearch_to_tsquery parses the keyword search query the way a person types into a search box

cases.question: What does MAX_DOCX_UNCOMPRESSED_SIZE_BYTES protect against?
expected_facts: It bounds a DOCX file's decompressed size to guard against a zip-bomb

cases.question: What is ix_document_chunks_embedding_cosine?
expected_facts: It is the ivfflat index on the embedding column used for vector search

cases.question: Walk through everything that happens from when a user uploads a document to when it becomes searchable.
expected_facts: The file is stored and a document row is inserted as PROCESSING
A Celery task is queued and a worker parses, chunks, and embeds the content
Chunks and embeddings are written to Postgres and the document is marked READY

cases.question: What design choices keep a slow LLM call from tying up resources needed by other requests?
expected_facts: Long-running work is not held in one giant transaction; each step commits incrementally
A database connection is not held open during LLM generation or streaming

cases.question: What steps does Retriva take to keep uploaded files from being a security risk?
expected_facts: File content is validated by sniffing actual bytes, not trusting the extension
Uploads are size-limited and parser-level limits guard against pathological documents
Storage keys are server-generated, never derived from the client filename

cases.question: How would you trace a slow retrieval step in Jaeger, and what span would you look for?
expected_facts: The rag.retrieval span (and its rag.vector_search/rag.keyword_search children) shows retrieval timing in Jaeger

cases.question: How is document processing represented in distributed tracing?
expected_facts: Document ingestion has a document.processing span with document.parse/.chunk/.embed/.persist children

cases.question: Is the streaming chat endpoint subject to rate limiting?
expected_facts: Chat and chat/stream are both rate-limited via RATE_LIMIT_CHAT_PER_MINUTE

cases.question: What is a fused_score in Retriva's retrieval system?
expected_facts: fused_score is the RRF ranking score combining vector and keyword rank, used only for ordering, not as a probability

cases.question: What does 'time to first token' mean in Retriva's streaming system?
expected_facts: Time to first token is the delay between the stream starting and the first generated token arriving

cases.question: What is the difference between a request ID and a trace ID in Retriva?
expected_facts: A request ID is an app-level correlation identifier returned to the client
A trace ID is OpenTelemetry's distributed tracing identifier used to look up spans in Jaeger

cases.question: What is RETRIEVAL_MIN_SIMILARITY?
expected_facts: It's a confidence threshold on the best raw vector similarity, used to decide when evidence is insufficient

cases.question: What GPU model does Retriva require for running its embedding model?
cases.notes: The docs describe an embedding model (nomic-embed-text) and local/free infrastructure, but never specify or require any particular GPU hardware - a system fooled by keyword overlap on 'embedding'/'model' might fabricate a GPU answer.

cases.question: How much does Retriva charge per API call?
cases.notes: The docs describe a zero-cost, no-paid-API architecture but never state a per-call price - 'API' overlaps heavily with real content without answering this question.

cases.question: What production traffic volume was RRF_K's value of 60 empirically tuned against?
cases.notes: RRF_K=60 is documented as the standard constant from the original RRF paper, explicitly not empirically tuned against this project's traffic - a system that invents a tuning story here is fabricating, not retrieving.

cases.question: What is Retriva's pricing model for enterprise customers?
cases.notes: Not covered by any fixture document - out of domain entirely.

cases.question: Who is the CEO of Retriva?
cases.notes: The fixture corpus is technical documentation with no company/personnel information.

cases.question: Does Retriva support deployment on Kubernetes?
cases.notes: Only Docker Compose is documented; Kubernetes is never mentioned.

cases.question: What mobile apps does Retriva offer?
cases.notes: Only a Next.js web frontend is documented; no mobile app exists in any fixture document.

cases.question: What about full-text search?
history: What technology does Retriva use for vector similarity search?
expected_facts: Retriva uses PostgreSQL's native full-text search, not a separate search engine
cases.notes: The raw follow-up question has almost no lexical/semantic overlap with the answer on its own - it depends on the prior turn to resolve 'what about' into 'what does Retriva use for full-text search'.

cases.question: What about session tokens?
expected_facts: Sessions use a JWT access token plus an opaque refresh token, both HTTP-only cookies

cases.question: Can it be retried?
history: What happens when a document fails to process?
expected_facts: A failed document can be retried, which re-queues it for processing
